## Before you build

Use this quick reference alongside the **Lab 3 Video Guide: Tableau and Excel**
in Canvas. The videos show the full click-by-click walkthrough; these hints
show where fields go and which transformations to check.

Connect to `chicago_traffic_crashes_sample.csv`. Keep `crash_id` as text,
`crash_datetime` as date/time, and weather measurements and coordinates as
numbers with decimal precision. Assign Latitude and Longitude geographic
roles to the matching coordinate fields.

**Crash count** below means Tableau's generated table **Count** measure.
Place it on **Text** in a blank sheet: the unfiltered total should be **12,000**.
Do not sum `crash_id`. Each row is one sampled crash.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" icon="false" title="Read the pill before the chart"}
Check the aggregation (Count, SUM, or AVG), date level, and filters on each
sheet. Blue means discrete and green means continuous; this is separate from
dimension versus measure. Keep sheet-specific filters local.
:::

## 1) Ranking

**Question:** Which reported causes appear most often?

| Tableau location | Field or setting |
|---|---|
| Rows | `primary_contributory_cause` |
| Columns | Crash count |
| Marks | Bar; crash count on Label if useful |
| Filters | Exclude missing causes, UNABLE TO DETERMINE, and NOT APPLICABLE |

**Transform:** Sort by count descending. Select the ten largest remaining bars
and **Keep Only**, as in the demo. This is a fixed selection, not a dynamic
Top N rule.

**Check:** Ten causes remain; bar lengths are crash counts. Keep this selection
on Ranking only.

## 2) Nominal comparison

**Question:** How does average injury count differ across causes?

| Tableau location | Field or setting |
|---|---|
| Rows | `primary_contributory_cause` |
| Columns | `AVG(injuries_total)` |
| Marks | Bar; crash count on Tooltip |
| Filters | Crash count: **At least 30**; exclude NOT APPLICABLE |

**Transform:** Duplicate Ranking, then **remove its cause selection**. Replace
count with `injuries_total`, change **Measure > Average**, and sort by average.

**Check:** The pill says AVG, not SUM. Label the axis **Average injuries per
crash**. Inspect the count behind an average; the 30-crash cutoff does not
make every group equally reliable.

## 3) Time series

**Question:** How do monthly crash counts change over time?

| Tableau location | Field or setting |
|---|---|
| Columns | `crash_datetime`: continuous **Month** (green) |
| Rows | Crash count |
| Marks | Line; `reported_weather_condition` on Color |
| Filters | Exclude CLEAR to match the saved demo; UNKNOWN is an optional exclusion |

**Transform:** Use month-year positions on a continuous timeline. A discrete
month name can combine January across different years.

**Check:** Dates run chronologically across years. State which weather
conditions were excluded; counts in this sample are not crash rates.

## 4) Part-to-whole

**Question:** Within each quarter, what share belongs to each injury category?

| Tableau location | Start with a text table | Then make stacked bars |
|---|---|---|
| Columns | `crash_datetime`: discrete **Quarter** (blue) | Keep Quarter |
| Rows | `most_severe_injury` | Crash count with Percent of Total |
| Marks | Crash count on Text | Bar; `most_severe_injury` on Color |
| Filters | Exclude null injury categories | Keep the same exclusion |

**Transform:** Apply **Quick Table Calculation > Percent of Total** to count.
In the text table, compute **Table (Down)**. After moving fields, recheck:
address `most_severe_injury` and partition by Quarter using **Specific
Dimensions**. The denominator is the included crashes within each quarter.

**Check:** Every complete quarter totals approximately 100%. Discrete Q1-Q4
combines the same quarter across years.

::: {.callout-important appearance="minimal" icon="false" title="Hide is different from Exclude"}
First verify the complete 100% stacks. Then practice **Hide** on NO INDICATION
OF INJURY and REPORTED, NOT EVIDENT, as in the demo. They still contribute to
the table-calculation denominator, so visible portions total less than 100%.
**Exclude** would instead recalculate shares among remaining records. Label
the reduced display and show hidden categories again to check the full total.
:::

## 5) Relationship

**Question:** How are temperature and dew point related?

| Tableau location | Field or setting |
|---|---|
| Columns | `weather_station_name`, then `temperature_f` |
| Rows | `dew_point_f` |
| Marks | Circle; reduce opacity |
| Filters | Exclude null station names |

**Transform:** Turn off **Analysis > Aggregate Measures** for individual
observations, matching the demo. Alternatively, a unique `crash_id` on Detail
separates crashes while keeping aggregation on.

**Check:** You should see many marks, not a single SUM point. Label both axes
in degrees F. Several crashes can share the same station-hour observation.

## 6) Distribution

**Question:** How does temperature vary across reported weather conditions?

| Tableau location | Histogram exploration | Box-plot comparison |
|---|---|---|
| Columns | `temperature_f (bin)` | `temperature_f` |
| Rows | Crash count | `reported_weather_condition` |
| Marks | Bar | Individual observations with a box plot |

**Transform:** Select temperature and use **Show Me > Histogram**; edit its bin
size (try 5 degrees F). For box plots, start a fresh sheet, turn off
**Aggregate Measures** or add `crash_id` to Detail, then add **Box Plot** from
Analytics. Keep the histogram on a duplicate sheet if desired.

**Check:** Box plots summarize individual observations, not one average per
category. Compare medians, the middle 50%, spread, and unusual points. Use
`temperature_f`, not visibility, for this demo.

## 7) Map

**Question:** Where are the sampled crashes located?

| Tableau location | Field or setting |
|---|---|
| Columns | `longitude` |
| Rows | `latitude` |
| Marks | Map/circle; `crash_id` on Detail; `trafficway_type` on Color |

**Transform:** Keep aggregation on and use the crash ID to separate marks,
as in the completed workbook. Adjust size and opacity. A ZIP-code filled map
is an optional extension; it changes a mark from a crash to an area.

**Check:** Points fall around Chicago. Investigate null coordinates. Document
any subset filter; more sampled crashes does not automatically mean greater
risk per traveler.

## Excel reminders

Reproduce at least three views using matching filters and aggregations.

- **Ranking:** PivotTable Rows = cause; Values = **Count of crash_id**.
- **Nominal:** Rows = cause; Values = **Average of injuries_total** plus crash
  count. Use the same count-at-least-30 and NOT APPLICABLE restrictions.
- **Time:** Group dates by **Years and Months**; Values = crash count.
- **Relationship:** Use a regular **XY Scatter** chart of raw temperature (X)
  and dew point (Y), not a PivotChart.

## Final check

- Save Tableau as a packaged **`.twbx`** and Excel as **`.xlsx`**; reopen both.
- Check seven Tableau views and at least three Excel views against the lab prompt.
- Give charts question-based titles and axes meaningful units.
- Explain what one mark represents, what each percentage divides by, and which
  filters or hidden categories affect the display.
- Use **Lab3_Completed.twbx** in the Canvas Week 3 module to compare field
  placements and settings with the in-class example.
